STEP 1 - Scene: A single slice of pepperoni pizza (thin-to-medium crust, cheese, four-plus pepperoni rounds, some browned crust edges) on a plate.

STEP 2 - Vessel: White square-ish dinner/side plate, roughly 26 cm across. Area ≈ 3.14 × (13)² ≈ 530 cm². The pizza slice is the only food on this plate.

STEP 3 - Items: (a) pizza crust, (b) melted mozzarella cheese, (c) pepperoni slices (about 4 large, 1 partial visible).

STEP 4 - Area: The slice spans roughly a triangular/wedge shape of about 200 cm² total area in the photo, which is ~38% of the plate. Split: crust ~10% (about 53 cm²), cheese and sauce base ~18% (about 95 cm²), pepperoni ~10% (about 53 cm²). Total ≈ 38%, consistent with the visible coverage.

STEP 5 - Volume:
- Crust: 53 cm² × 1.5 cm ≈ 80 ml
- Cheese/sauce layer: 95 cm² × 0.6 cm ≈ 57 ml
- Pepperoni: 53 cm² × 0.4 cm ≈ 21 ml

STEP 6 - Grams (bulk density):
- Crust (bread-like, ~0.9 g/ml, but baked crust is airier, so ~0.5 effective): 80 ml → ~40 g... using the given bread-like range, I take 0.6 for pizza crust given its open crumb: ≈ 48 g
- Cheese/sauce: 57 ml × 1.0 ≈ 57 g
- Pepperoni: 21 ml × 0.9 ≈ 19 g

Total ≈ 124 g.

STEP 7 - Energy:
- Pizza crust (baked, ~270 kcal/100 g): 48 g → 130 kcal
- Mozzarella/cheese with tomato base (~280 kcal/100 g): 57 g → 160 kcal
- Pepperoni (~490 kcal/100 g): 19 g → 93 kcal

Total ≈ 383 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: A standard slice of pepperoni pizza is typically 100–150 g and 250–350 kcal. The estimate of ~124 g and ~380 kcal is plausible, perhaps slightly high on energy given the fairly generous cheese and pepperoni visible, so I keep it as estimated.

Summary: about 125 g, about 380 kcal.
